description: Synthetic register map served by the loopback DUT (NUCLEO-H533RE) responders; source: loopback_dut/docs/PROTOCOL.md §4 (DUT fw 0.2, protocol 1). Multi-address file: R1 = I2C2 at 0x6B (word base 0xA000), R2 = I2C3 at 0x55 (word base 0xB000); rules carry their own address and the Registers tab shows one tab per responder (address_names). Word region: word(p) = base + p, little-endian, so a read shows the responder base in the high byte (A0 = R1, B0 = R2; a wrong base means a mis-routed phase) and the pointer echo in the low byte (must equal the register). Writes are acknowledged and counted but NOT stored, so read values never change; the 'writes (last value)' panes show what the host last wrote. R1 has the TI BQ769x-style subcommand block at 0x3E..0x61 (echo, checksum and length are checked by the engine; a mismatch is flagged with a warning sign). Addresses are rig.toml defaults; if rig.toml changes them, this file must change too. Test fixture for the loopback harness, not a real device. 0x6B also belongs to bq25731_decoder.json: load only one of the two (same-address cross-talk is review B19). Layout v2 (2026-10-05): per-responder panes, word fields, write and block panes.

rules.name: R1 word 0x00
rules.description: Word region: word(0x00) = 0xA000 + 0x00 = 0xA000, LE (loopback_dut/docs/PROTOCOL.md §4). Longer reads decode the first word only.

fields.name: word
fields.description: 16-bit value = 0xA000 + pointer (little-endian)

fields.name: base
fields.description: responder base: 0xA0 expected; another value means the phase reached the wrong responder

fields.name: pointer
fields.description: pointer echo: must equal the register written just before the read

rules.name: LB simple write
rules.description: 1-byte write with STOP and no read (pattern case LB-04, review B8). On the DUT this byte is the pointer (loopback_dut/docs/PROTOCOL.md §4); the rule exists so a correct stream decoder renders 'LB simple write = 0x20'. There is intentionally NO indexed rule at 0x20, the B8 fix condition.

rules.name: LB block 0x0001
rules.description: Subcommand 0x0001 written to 0x3E; block read from 0x3E returns echo 01 00, buf[i] = (0x40+i) XOR 0x01, checksum 0x0E, length 36 (loopback_dut/docs/PROTOCOL.md §4). Case LB-09.
